Hannah / Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. AppScale's infra team wants a concise, executable plan to compare Redwood vs the two hyperscaler inference endpoints we mentioned (HyperCloud API and FastServe). Our goals:

- Confirm p95/p99 latency differences for our typical prompt mix (50–300 tokens).
- Measure sustained tokens/sec (tokens/s) under 4 concurrent client patterns we use.

Ethan — thanks for the clear list. Attached are three artifacts to get started: benchmark-config.yaml (test definitions), sample_prompt_set.csv (your prompts anonymized), and a comparison matrix we maintain. Below is a concise proposal to keep the window small and results actionable.

Proposed A/B matrix (high level):
- A: Redwood (default FP16 runtime)
- B: Redwood (int8 quant profile)
- C: HyperCloud API (latest stable)
- D: FastServe (v2)

Test knobs / notes:
- Workload slices: 1) short (50–80 tokens), 2) medium (150–220), 3) long (400–512)
- Client patterns: single client steady qps, 4 concurrent clients bursty, 10 concurrent ramp to saturation, cold-start spike (KV empty)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (generation end), 95th token latency, sustained tokens/s (measured at service edge), error rates, and cost/tokens (rough)
- Measurement method: run three 10-minute trials per slice, discard first 60s as warmup, report median of trials. We'll capture CPU/GPU utilization and KV hit rates.

Hypotheses we expect to validate:
1) Redwood quant profile will keep p95 within 10% of FP16 while improving tokens/s by ~1.6x on our benchmark nodes.
2) Hyperscaler endpoints show competitive single-request p50 but degrade more under concurrent sustained tokens/s patterns.
3) Cold KV scenarios increase p99 significantly; caching policies will be a primary driver.

Logistics and ownership:
- Redwood (Hannah / Ben): produce the benchmark-config.yaml and runner containers + a short README for your infra team to execute in staging.
- AppScale (Ethan): provide short-lived staging creds OR confirm if you prefer Redwood to run the tests from a Redwood-managed staging tenant using anonymized data.
- Redwood (Jordan): coordinate results dashboard delivery and a 30-minute readout the week after the runs.

Timeline (proposed):
- Today (Aug 29): confirm plan and VPC feasibility
- Aug 30–31: test execution window (you run or we run — TBD)
- Sep 1–2: analysis and one-page readout, deliver p95/p99 charts + tokens/s curves

Deliverables we will attach/send: raw runner logs, Grafana p95/p99 panels, cost model appendix.

If you confirm VPC execution is required, we can send a short checklist for network allow-listing and a signed NDA addendum for test artifacts.

Thanks — assigning Ben to the runner build (attached config) and Jordan will pick up dashboards.

Hannah Schmitt
VP, Applied Performance
Redwood Inference
